full_judgment: 8. I have perused the materials on record and considered the submissions of the learned Counsel of the petitioner. 5 PWs and 3 DWs have been examined. On careful reading of the statements of the witnesses and judgments of the Courts below, it appeared to me that both the Courts below committed error in considering the facts, law related to this case and sifting properly the statement of the witnesses of both sides though the witnesses deposed supporting their respective cases. The trial Judge did not at all consider the position of the plaintiff No. 1 who was a proforma defendant No. 9 in title Suit No. 44 of 1942 and defendant No. 1 in title Suit No. 60 of 1966 was an illiterate man and even he did not know how to sign, then how he could put signature on the vokalatnama, written statement and Rafanama. The defendant did not cross-examine the PW 1 and other PWs on the point to find out that the plaintiff No. 1 Ana Miah Patwary was a literate man how he could sign. But the Subordinate Judge did not take any pain to ascertain the matter but he ought to have come to the findings that the plaintiff did not have the knowledge of TS No. 44 of 1942 and TS No. 60 of 1966 but the Subordinate Judge, acted most illegally for which the judgment and decree should be set aside and the plaintiffs suit be decreed. The same error was also committed by the appellate Court. The argument advanced by the learned Counsel has also legal value that the defendant claimed the suit land through a pattanama which was executed and registered by landlord's predecessors of the plaintiff Noor Jahan Begum and Asamuddin Patwary granting some lands to Ashraf Ali Bepari and Yosuf Ali Bepari. In the putta the Zamindars (who were also illiterate) reserved the right of transfer by the pattandars in favour of the Zamindars or their heirs and none else. The transfer by the Pattandars or by their heirs are prohibited. In the pattan name the transfer made by the pattandar or their heirs are illegal and void and by the transfer of the pattandars or their heirs the transferees got no title in the property. This aspect of law has not been taken into consideration by the Courts below which is vital point of law. On the basis of above facts I find perverse in the judgment of the Courts below, non-reading of the statements of the witnesses and wrong explanation of Municipal Law related to the case. So, the judgments of the Courts below should be interfered by invoking revisional jurisdiction. The references given by the learned Counsel are also applicable in the case and his submission of learned Counsel has also substance and force. The Rule has merit.
